title: P-53 Mutation GA-SOM Analysis
description: Combines genetic algorithms simulating <inode id="mitosis-tree">mitotic propagation</inode> with self-organizing map clustering to identify <inode id="high-risk-pentamers">six pentamer motifs</inode> that consistently precede malignant P-53 mutations.

ncbi-strand-curation.title: NCBI Strand Curation
ncbi-strand-curation.description: 25 wild-type and cancerous P-53 DNA strands of 2,509 bases each were pulled from NCBI, stripped of non-nucleotide characters, and aligned into parental/pathological pairs.

mitosis-tree.title: Generative Mitosis Tree
mitosis-tree.description: A binary tree models mitotic bifurcation across 14 generations, with each node storing its generation index, DNA composition, and malignancy state to emulate tumour initiation depth.

levenshtein-drift-scoring.title: Levenshtein Drift Scoring
levenshtein-drift-scoring.description: Depth-first traversal of the <inode id="mitosis-tree">generative mitosis tree</inode> extracts generational paths and scores mismatch rates via Levenshtein similarity, flagging the highest-drift ancestors that precede malignant nodes.

kmer-vectors.title: k-mer Feature Vectors
kmer-vectors.description: Using k = 4 (from log base 4 of sequence length), each strand is transformed into a 1x1024 nucleotide-frequency vector, yielding 73,475 length-adjusted rows.

1x6-lattice-selection.title: 1x6 Lattice Selection
1x6-lattice-selection.description: SOM grids from 1x2 to 1x11 were compared against the <inode id="kmer-vectors">k-mer frequency vectors</inode>, with correlation analysis reducing redundancy before settling on a 1x6 lattice that reached the best 0.451 silhouette score.

high-risk-pentamers.title: Six High-Risk Pentamers
high-risk-pentamers.description: The winning lattice separated six thymine-heavy pentamer motifs (cagcc, agcca, cccag, ccagg, ttttt, ctttt) that consistently appear in malignant branches.

pathway-dependent-progression.title: Pathway-Dependent Progression
pathway-dependent-progression.description: Each of the six clusters carries a distinct nucleotide fingerprint, indicating that mutation progression toward malignancy follows structured pathways rather than random drift.
